Judgments rest on the page layout and what each row actually says.

**Page 41 (diagnostic mammogram, items 0, 1, 13, 20).** The "$0 copay for each diagnostic mammogram" text sits in the Breast cancer screening row, which is a Medicare-covered benefit. Item 1 gives the unit "per visit", but the quote says "each diagnostic mammogram", so item 1 is false. Items 0, 13 and 20 are acceptable. Item 20 says "per mammogram", which is close enough to "per diagnostic mammogram". Item 13 has no unit and is fine.

**Page 58 (outpatient diagnostic tests and supplies, setting "any").**
- X-ray is $15 per x-ray. Item 9 (no unit) and item 16 (per x-ray) are true. Item 18 says "per visit", which the quote does not support, so it is false.
- CT is $350 per CT scan. Item 2 (per CT scan), item 4 (no unit) and item 10 (per scan) are true. Item 19 says "per visit" and is false.
- Diagnostic radiology other than CT is $350 per service. Item 3 is false because it uses "per visit". Items 24 and 25 are true.
- Item 5 uses the benefit `imaging.diagnostic` with $350, and its quotes include both the CT and the non-CT lines. Both are $350, so it is consistent, but the CT line belongs to a different benefit. The "diagnostic" benefit is defined as other than X-rays and priced together, and CT counts as advanced imaging within it, so a combined $350 is accurate. I accept it.

**Page 60 (outpatient hospital services, setting `outpatient_hospital`).**
- X-ray is $15. Item 6 (per x-ray) and item 22 (no unit) are true. Item 11 says "per visit" and is false.
- CT is $350. Item 7 (per CT scan), item 12 (per scan) and item 15 (no unit) are true. Item 14 says "per visit" and is false.
- Diagnostic radiology other than CT is $350. Item 8 (per diagnostic radiology service) and item 21 (per service) are true. Item 17 says "per visit" and is false.
- Item 23 has no unit and combines both quotes, as item 5 does, and is true.
